## Analysis at each round
### Round 1
There are no trials yet. The starting architecture scored 0.000 on both seeds. With the default recipe it gets only 32 updates (131k steps at 4 PPO epochs), which is probably far too few to learn exact multi-brick builds. Its footprint pooling head already gives it the right tools to estimate where a brick lands and whether it covers missing cells, so too few samples and updates seem a more likely cause of failure than too little capacity. Lowering the PPO epochs raises the sample count (2 epochs gives 1.86x the samples, 1 epoch gives 3.25x), and a smaller n_envs gives many more updates. This round compares two such recipes on the unchanged network. The third candidate uses the 2-epoch recipe with a modestly deeper network that also passes a whole-board summary back into every cell (about 1.3x the compute), so comparing it with candidate 1 shows the effect of the network alone. Because the baseline is 0, any nonzero 2-seed score is informative.

### Round 2
All four runs so far, the baseline plus three in round 1, scored 0 on dev, and training success in the last 10% of training was also 0. Changing PPO epochs, sample count, number of updates, gamma or adding a third conv with global context did nothing. More samples or capacity on this flat 2D design does not seem to be enough. A placement is correct when every cell under the brick's footprint is still missing at the layer where the brick lands, which is the highest build height under that footprint, and no missing cell below gets covered. Working out the landing layer and then checking the target at that same layer is a two-step, layer-by-layer calculation. A network that merges all layers into channels before pooling over the footprint finds this hard to learn. This round tests that idea: run the trunk once per layer, giving each layer its own cells, its whole column and a one-hot layer code. Then score each footprint at each layer with min/max/average pooling and combine the layers with a soft maximum (logsumexp). Two candidates use the per-layer network with different recipes; one adds only a per-layer scoring head to the 2D baseline.

### Round 3
All 6 trials score exactly 0, on dev and in training (train success in the last 10% of training is also 0). The changes so far covered epochs (1, 2 or 4), more samples, a deeper trunk with global context, and per-layer heads. None moved the score. Even small 6-brick designs never get built during training, which is suspicious. Every network so far assumes that the logit at a cell's position places a brick anchored at that same cell, using local convolutions and footprint pooling. The task warns that the world may not behave as described. If the action indexing or the anchor convention differs (for example x and y swapped, or a different corner as anchor), local convolutional heads cannot learn the remapping, which would explain zero training success. This round tests heads that do not assume this alignment: a dense head added to the baseline, a transformer with learned positions, and a pure MLP. Time and compute are far from binding, at 75 to 215 seconds out of 900.

### Round 4
All 9 trials scored 0 on dev and 0 in training. That covers the baseline conv net, recipes with 1 or 2 epochs, deeper trunks, per-layer heads, dense remapping heads, a transformer and a flat MLP. Because the MLP and the dense heads also failed, a mismatch between the action grid and the observation grid is unlikely to be the only cause. The common factor is the recipe. Every run used gamma 0.95 or 0.97, entropy 0.005 to 0.01, and either 2 epochs with batch 2048 or 1 epoch with batch 4096. No run tested high gamma, high entropy, small batches or many updates. The remaining bottlenecks are probably exploration and credit assignment: the +1 exact-build bonus and a correctly timed DONE are far apart and rare. With only success numbers to go on, I cannot tell which hidden twist applies. This last round therefore spends the trials on untested recipe settings (gamma 0.99, entropy 0.02 to 0.03, smaller and more frequent updates) and on one new trunk with a wider view of the board.
